newsitem.title: USA: Ark gaming petition goes before court again Monday.
newsitem.headline: Ark gaming petition goes before court again Monday.

text.p: An Arkansas gambling amendment stricken from the November ballot earlier this week is expected to be submitted to the state Supreme Court Monday for a rehearing, a court official said.

Daniel Dodson, deputy clerk for the Arkansas State Supreme Court and Court of Appeals, said while the matter would "probably be submitted to the court on Monday," it is uncertain whether the court will announce its decision that day.
"That could be at any time," he said. "That's something we don't know until they bring it in to us."

Last Monday, the Arkansas Supreme Court ruled four to three to remove the amendment, Amendment 7, from the general election ballot due to ballot title problems. That same day, Amendment 7 backers said they would petition both for a rehearing and to have Special Justice Sandra Smith Hochstetter removed from the case.
Rehearing petitions were due by Friday.

A release issued by the Committee to Promote Arkansas, which supports Amendment 7, claims Hochstetter should be disqualified because of a "perceived conflict of interest." The release said Hochstetter is assistent general counsel for a business called Arkla Gas, which is represented by the law firm of Friday Eldredge & Clark.
The law firm also represents a competing Arkansas gambling amendment called Amendment 4.

A Friday Eldredge attorney who argued the Amendment 4 case before the court, also represents Arkla. The Committee to Promote Arkansas' release said Hochstetter cast the deciding vote to toss Amendment 7 from the ballot.
Hochstetter could not be reached for comment Thursday or Friday.
David Couch, an attorney with Dover & Dixon who represents Amendment 7, said the court's decision so close to Election Day leaves his client in a difficult position.

"My client's pulled his advertisement down right now based on the Supreme Court's decision," Couch said. "So we're really (in) a dead time right now, and it's really handcuffed us from getting our message out."
Amendment 7 was one of three gambling amendments removed from the Arkansas ballot Monday, making Amendment 4 the sole remaining gaming amendment.
